message: The cost catalogue's price rows are country-specific, and the brief names no country. Which region should the price rows assume? The rows available are: electricity and gas — Netherlands (Eurostat NL non-household, 2024 S2); heat revenue — Netherlands (NL regulated household ceiling 2026, NL DH tariff 2021) or Sweden (SE DH tariff 2021); cold revenue — Norway (district cooling average) or EU27 (customer's own cooling, 2014); carbon price — EU ETS (EU-wide); discount rate — Netherlands (PBL SDE++ 2025 geothermal WACC, real). Please name the region (e.g. Netherlands, Sweden, EU-wide) so I know which rows to recommend.

The brief gives no site location, no outside-air data, no return temperatures and no utility data. Please give me these case values (each with its unit), and confirm the two sourced values at the end:

1. site.air.temperature — °C, the outside air temperature (constant is fine). Needed for the air-side of coolers/heat pumps and for the plant's ambient losses.
2. site.air.relative_humidity — a fraction 0-1 (e.g. 0.8, not 80 %). Needed for the cooling tower / dew-point check.
3. site.air.pressure — Pa, bar or kPa, OR the site's elevation in m (I will then let gemini set the ISA pressure). Needed for air density.
4. demand.heating.return_temperature — °C, the temperature the heating water returns at; must be colder than the 100 °C supply the brief fixes.
5. demand.cooling.return_temperature — °C, the temperature the chilled water returns at; must be warmer than the 20 °C supply the brief fixes.
6. site.fluid.sand_concentration — the produced brine's sand/solids content with its unit (e.g. g/m3 or ppm); the report's brine table gives none. Needed for the solids handling and erosion check.

To confirm (values I took from the knowledge base, not from your files):
A. time_zone = UTC for both demand files — the CSVs' dates carry no offset, and gemini reads offset-less dates as UTC; this is my assumption, not your choice.
B. utilities.electricity.co2_intensity = 209.21 g/kWh — Ember Yearly Electricity Data, EU power-sector CO2 intensity 2025, catalogue row co2-grid-eu-2025 (verified).

You may answer "approve A and B" and give the six values, or change any of them.

Two confirmations before the economics:

1. site.air.pressure — from your 100 m elevation, gemini set the ISA (ISO 2533:1975) pressure to 100129.43746672753 Pa. Confirm this value?
2. The two demand CSVs' date column has no time offset, so gemini reads the series as UTC. Is UTC the right time zone for the demand series (the brief's dates are bare dates and name no zone)?

Economics of the case, from the cost catalogue.
Region as you instructed: the Netherlands for electricity, gas, heat revenue and the discount rate; EU-wide for the carbon price; the EU27 row for cold revenue. No subsidy: the four revenue.subsidy keys are left open and unset, as you asked. The catalogue has no per-energy O&M row for any chiller, so the three chiller keys are open: a plant that uses a chiller needs your price per MWh of cold, or the per-energy map cannot price it. Heat revenue: the NL 2026 row is a regulated household ceiling (an upper bound, incl. VAT), so the NL 2021 district-heating tariff is recommended and the ceiling is shown beside it. Drilling: the three NL rows are the same year, so the middle value (3000 m) is recommended; the site's reservoir midpoint is 2500 m. If a production-pump row is recommended, note the catalogue's ESP rows are per W electric (motor rating) while the key is per W of shaft power: shaft power is about 0.85 to 0.9 of the electric rating, so per W of shaft power the cost is about 10 to 15 % higher.
